text:
acme-platform: hey @sophia-support — our customer acme-prod-42 saw 429s right after their monthly tokens were supposed to refill. UI showed the new balance at local midnight (PST) but API kept rejecting streaming reconnects. when are tokens actually usable?
sophia-support: sorry about the disruption. can you paste tenant id and when you first saw 429s? did the 429 responses include a Retry-After? :thinking:
acme-platform: tenant=acme-prod-42. first 429 at 2024-11-01T00:02:12Z. curl of the stream start returned `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` plus `Retry-After: 120`. UI text said "Refilled 00:00 PST — 10,000 tokens".
devon-engineer: are you hitting with an org-level key or a project/service token? org keys consume the org-monthly pool and have slightly different enforcement behavior.
acme-platform: org key. no subscription change.
sophia-support: quick notes: (1) the dashboard view is served from CDN/edge caches and can show the new balance slightly earlier than enforcement nodes, (2) the canonical refill event is applied at the core store at the monthly boundary (by default 00:00 UTC unless tenant configured for a local boundary), (3) aggressive client reconnects after a refill can deplete burst and trigger throttles again while caches and smoothing windows sync.
acme-platform: repro from our side: keep a streaming session open, force a connection drop, then retry immediately 3x with no backoff. each reconnect consumes tokens and we saw the bucket show as 0 then UI flip to 10k but API still 429 on the reconnect attempts.
devon-engineer: yep — each reconnect is treated as a new consumption. the enforcement layer uses admission checks that may consult slightly stale replicas; Retry-After is set by the smoothing algorithm. if you blast retries you get penalized with conservative Retry-After values.
kai-oncall: looked at infra: core shows refill at 2024-11-01T00:00:00Z (tokens_before=0 tokens_after=10000). some edge nodes had stale cache entries for ~40s which explains the mismatch. excerpt from logs:
```
2024-11-01T00:00:00Z core refill tenant=acme-prod-42 tokens_before=0 tokens_after=10000
2024-11-01T00:00:02Z edge-cache-get tenant=acme-prod-42 value=0 ttl_remaining=38s
```
kai-oncall: Retry-After:120 looks like the computed smoothing period for rapid reconnect patterns — it's not the time until the monthly refill.
sophia-support: we can push a targeted patch: drop edge cache TTL on refill for this tenant to ~5s and relax smoothing for the immediate 2m after refill so clients don't get long Retry-After windows. want us to apply it?
acme-platform: please do. customer needs minimal interruption during the boundary. also can billing double-check no proration or accidental plan change removed the tokens? they were worried they "lost" credits.
billing-bot: opened ticket SUP-31245 for billing validation on tenant=acme-prod-42. we'll confirm plan events around 2024-11-01.
ai-monitor-bot: alert generated: P2 throttle spike for acme-prod-42 at monthly boundary.
sophia-support: hotfix applied: reduced refill cache TTL to 5s and softened throttle smoothing window for acme-prod-42. monitor and report if 429s persist.
acme-platform: saw a handful (~3-6) more 429s across ~30s then cleared; UI and API matched within a minute. thanks.
devon-engineer: longer-term suggestions: prefer per-project service tokens for critical streams to avoid org-pool contention, add exponential backoff + jitter to clients on reconnect, and use connection-idempotency so retries can be deduped server-side. we'll log a runtime ticket to improve the refill push to hot nodes at boundary time.
sophia-support: we'll assemble a short postmortem + recommended client-side changes and link infra/billing tickets. :thumbsup: 
acme-platform: appreciate it. please include example client reconnection backoff code in the notes.
billing-bot: SUP-31245 linked to support case #SUPPORT-7890.
sophia-support: closing here — reopen if you see regression after the hotfix.
